paragraphs.text: Live wallpaper layer for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — procedural presets, images, GIF and video be
hind a translucent shell
# dsh-lively

Live wallpaper layer for the **DeepSeek Harness Web GUI**: an animated wallpaper
behind the interfac

e — procedural presets, images, GIF or video — with a small
settings page to pick the look.
**▶ Watch the 47-second intro video** — narrated tour of the presets, custom wallpapers, playlist an
d controls (1080p30, Chinese narration).
## Features

- **Six procedural presets** — Flow, Aurora, Starfield, Lava, Mesh, Neon grid.
Flow is the deliberat

ely animated one (position + size drift); each preset has
a dark variant for the dark palette and a

bright variant for the light
palette, so a light theme never ends up with a grey wash.
- **Custom wa

llpaper** — image, GIF, WebP, AVIF, MP4 or WebM, by URL or uploaded
from disk. Uploads live under `$

DSH_HOME/dsh-lively-media/` and are served by
the plugin's own route, so they survive a reload and a

restart.
- **Controls** — wallpaper strength (how much wallpaper shows through), dim,
video softnes

s, animation speed, a motion switch (the reduced-motion escape
hatch), pause when the window is hidd

en.
- **Playlist** — rotate through any subset of the presets every 1–240 minutes,
in order or shuff

led.
- **Wallpaper library** — every uploaded file is listed in Settings, so a
wallpaper picked last

week is one click away; the host lists
`$DSH_HOME/dsh-lively-media/` through `/dsh-lively/library`.

- **Theme aware** — the veil is keyed on `body[data-ds-dark-theme]`; the
bright/dark preset variant
s are keyed on `html:has(> body[data-ds-dark-theme])`.
## Install
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then restart DSH (the sidebar's restart button, if installed) and open
**Settings → Live wallpaper**

hen restart DSH (the sidebar's restart button, if installed) and open
**Settings → Live wallpaper**.
## How it works

- The wallpaper lives in one fixed layer at `z-index:-1` (`#dsh-lively-layer`)
with three children:

the animated **surface**, the theme-coloured **veil**
(`strength`) and the **dim** overlay. The laye

r is appended to the root so it
sits under every column.
- Why not the root element's own background

? Chromium paints the root background
into the canvas background layer; a `background-position`/`bac

kground-size`
animation on `html` advances the animation clock but does not repaint on
screen, so th

e presets looked static. An ordinary element repaints, and that
is what the layer uses.
- The shell

paints `--dsw-alias-bg-base` on the frame *and* on the centre
column, and alphas multiply. The token

is therefore fully **transparent**, so
the layer shows through with the single veil painted once, a

bove the surface.
- No `backdrop-filter` on the shell columns: it would make them the containing
blo

ck for fixed-position descendants, and the sidebar's fold toggle is
`position: fixed` — frosting the

column drags that button onto the brand mark.
- Settings persist twice: `localStorage` (instant) an

d
`$DSH_HOME/dsh-lively-state.json` via `/dsh-lively/state`, because the Desktop
app's loopback port
changes on every launch.
## Limitations

- A video wallpaper needs a real `<video>` element; CSS alone cannot play video.
- The softness cont

rol applies to video only — CSS cannot blur the root
background, and blurring the columns breaks fix

ed-position shell chrome.
- The frame-transparency rule targets `[class$='_frame']`, which follows t

he
shell's CSS-module naming.
